count_policy: The canonical scan is reproducible and hash-checked; explicit cfg(test) module ranges are test_inline owned while ambiguous mixed-source items remain production owned.

commands: cargo clippy --locked -p nautilus-core -p nautilus-model -p nautilus-common -p nautilus-backtest --lib -- -D warnings
limitations: Dedicated tests, benches, test_kit, testing, stubs, tests.rs, and *_test.rs files are test-owned.
Generated and FFI paths are separate owners and are not mechanically rewritten.

Explicit cfg(test) module ranges in mixed source files are test_inline owned; the lexical range scanner handles nested block comments, quoted strings, raw strings, character literals, and nested braces.
Inline module declaration and closing-boundary lines remain production-owned because canonical rows are line-based and could contain production tokens outside the module boundary.
Standalone cfg(test) items and any unrecognized or ambiguous conditional syntax remain production-owned rather than risking false test classification.
Signal totals are line-based rather than call-based, so behavior-preserving formatting can merge or split textual signal rows without changing the number of Rust calls.

production.decision: Harden selected input and iterator boundaries; retain documented compatibility and construction invariants.

test.decision: Retain assertions and unwrap/expect calls used to make fixture failures immediate.

test_inline.decision: Retain explicit cfg(test) module assertions separately from production trends; ambiguous conditional items remain production-owned.

generated.decision: Retain generator-owned lint exceptions; changes must originate in the generator or schema.

ffi.decision: Retain ABI-owned unsafe and conversion invariants; require a dedicated FFI task and ABI fixtures for changes.

findings.risk: runtime iterator exhaustion could remain represented as Option while code used unwrap after a separate check
findings.result: let-else and Option::is_none_or remove both unwrap calls without recovery or retry

findings.risk: missing, non-finite, unstable, or incompatible points could panic before callers could fail closed
findings.result: checked try_* APIs return InterpolationError; existing panic APIs remain compatibility wrappers

findings.risk: runtime curve data has public vectors and can be missing, non-finite, or shape-incompatible
findings.result: try_get_rate provides structured fail-closed errors; cache ingestion validates curves and production Greeks lookups propagate checked errors; get_rate remains a compatibility wrapper
LiveNode build validates before conversion; changing From to TryFrom requires separate public-contract migration approval

findings.risk: cache read assumes the immediately preceding successful cache insertion is observable
findings.result: not selected because a meaningful negative test requires a dedicated cache fault-injection boundary

findings.risk: invalid external discriminants can panic through the compatibility constructor
findings.result: NodeState::try_from_u8 is the checked boundary; internal atomic values use enum discriminants

findings.risk: stored identifier is not currently read
findings.result: field is bounded reconciliation state and has no runtime failure behavior

findings.risk: mutability differs by plugin feature ownership
findings.result: cfg_attr applies only when plugin code is not compiled

findings.risk: comments identify future API or representation cleanup but do not execute
findings.result: no TODO macro or unimplemented runtime branch was selected

findings.path: dedicated tests, benches, test_kit, testing, stubs, tests.rs, and *_test.rs files
findings.risk: test failures intentionally stop the test
findings.result: dedicated test paths are separated from production; mixed src files remain conservatively production-owned

findings.risk: generated decoding shape and unused surfaces are schema-owned
findings.result: manual edits are prohibited; adapter changes require raw fixture coverage

findings.symbol: C ABI pointer and conversion surfaces
findings.risk: raw pointer and ABI representation contracts require dedicated ownership
findings.result: no unsafe or ABI code changed; Miri and sanitizer are not selected for this PR

findings.risk: extreme finite coordinates can overflow intermediate subtraction or polynomial terms
findings.result: coordinate scaling avoids finite-input subtraction overflow and every checked interpolation result rejects non-finite output

findings.path: mixed crates/**/src/*.rs files containing inline test modules
findings.risk: whole-file ownership inflated production trends, while an over-broad textual downgrade could hide later production code
findings.result: 10546 signals inside explicit cfg(test) module ranges are test_inline owned; 2702 remaining production signals and ambiguous cfg(test) items stay production-owned; a seven-case fixture verifies boundaries and precedence
